title: Mechanical spinal cord transection in larval zebrafish and subsequent whole-mount histological processing
protocol: Place larvae in lateral position on the surgery plate for perforation lesion preparation.
Perform spinal cord transection under visual control using a stereo microscope at high magnification.
Ensure complete transection of the spinal cord without notochord damage.
Maintain dorsal edge integrity for perforation lesions to facilitate histological processing.
Anesthetize zebrafish larvae (3 dpf) in E3 medium containing 0.02% Ethyl 3-aminobenzoate methanesulfonate (MS-222/Tricaine).
Place sufficiently anesthetized larvae on a surgery plate for preparation.
Prepare a recovery dish containing E3 medium without MS-222.
Add PTU to E3 medium before beginning the procedure.
Transfer anesthetized larvae to a surgery plate using a transfer pipette.
Remove excess E3 medium from the larvae using an aspiration pipette.
Approach the larva with the micro scalpel from the ventral side at the level of the urogenital pore.
Position the needle bevel facing up, towards the dorsal side of the larva.
Push the tip of the needle through the trunk immediately dorsal to the notochord to transect the spinal cord.
Take care to avoid injuring the notochord during the procedure.
Gently flush lesioned larvae off the surgery plate into the recovery dish using a transfer pipette filled with E3 medium.
Keep lesioned larvae in a 28.5°C incubator for recovery.
Remove sick and dead larvae on the same day and subsequently check lesioned larvae daily.
Approach the larva with the micro scalpel from the dorsal side, at the level of the urogenital pore.
Ensure the needle bevel is facing sideways.
Induce an incision into the dorsal trunk spanning from the notochord to the dorsal edge.
Avoid injuring the notochord during the incision.
Exclude larvae showing excessive damage to the notochord from further analysis.
Terminally anesthetize excluded larvae by adding MS-222 to E3 medium (final concentration ≥ 0.1%).
Gently flush lesioned larvae off the surgery plate into a recovery dish using a transfer pipette filled with E3 medium.
Keep lesioned larvae in a 28.5°C incubator for recovery.
Remove sick and dead larvae on the same day.
Check lesioned larvae daily subsequently.
Ensure sufficient volume of E3 medium remains on the surgery plate to prevent desiccation.
Fix zebrafish larvae with paraformaldehyde (PFA) after spinal cord lesion (0–2 days post-lesion; dpl).
Permeabilize fixed larvae.
Incubate permeabilized larvae with labeled antisense RNA probe to hybridize complementary mRNA sequences in cells expressing the corresponding gene.
Terminally anesthetize larvae by adding MS-222 to E3 medium (final concentration ≥ 0.1%).
Transfer larvae to a 2 mL reaction tube using a transfer pipette.
Fix larvae in 4% PFA at 4°C for 14–18 hours.
Wash larvae twice in PBST for 1 minute each.
Dehydrate larvae by incubating successively in 25% MeOH-PBST, 50% MeOH-PBST, 75% MeOH-PBST, and 100% MeOH for 5 minutes each.
Rehydrate samples by incubating successively in 75% MeOH-PBST, 50% MeOH-PBST, 25% MeOH-PBST, and PBST for 5 minutes each.
Wash larvae twice in PBST for 1 minute each.
Incubate larvae in PBST containing 40 μg/mL Proteinase K for 30 minutes.
Stop the Proteinase K digestion by washing larvae twice in PBST for less than or equal to 1 minute each.
Re-fix larvae by incubating in 4% PFA for 15 minutes.
Wash larvae five times in PBST for less than or equal to 1 minute each.
Incubate larvae in hybridization buffer (preheated to 66°C) for a minimum of 1 hour at 66°C.
Prepare hybridization mixes by combining 1 mL of hybridization buffer with 5 μL of RNA probe stock solution at a 1:200 dilution.
Preheat the hybridization mix to 66°C for 10 minutes on a thermomixer under vigorous shaking at ∼900 rpm.
Aspirate media and add 1 mL of preheated hybridization mix to each reaction tube.
Hybridize at 66°C in a water bath for 14–18 hours.
Wash samples in hybridization buffer at 66°C for 20 minutes.
Prepare SSCT/formamide mixture freshly.
Wash larvae 3× with the SSCT/formamide mixture at 66°C for 20 minutes each.
Wash larvae 2× in 2× SSCT buffer at 66°C for 20 minutes each.
Wash larvae 4× in 0.2× SSCT buffer at 66°C for 30 minutes each.
Wash larvae 2× in PBST for ≤1 minute each.
Incubate larvae in blocking solution for at least 1 hour.
Place the tubes on a see-saw rocking shaker with low agitation at approximately 10 rpm.
Dilute anti-digoxigenin-alkaline phosphatase antibody (anti-digoxigenin-AP) 1:3000 in blocking solution.
Incubate larvae in at least 1 mL of antibody solution at 4°C for 14–18 hours.
Wash larvae on a see-saw rocking shaker with low agitation at approximately 10 rpm using PBST twice for 1 minute each and six times for 20 minutes each.
Prepare NTMT staining buffer fresh.
Wash larvae in NTMT staining buffer twice for 5 minutes each to replace PBST and increase the pH to 9.0–9.5.
Dissolve one NBT/BCIP Ready-to-Use Tablet in 10 mL ddH2O, mix well.
Replace NTMT buffer with 1 mL staining solution to initiate the chromogenic reaction.
Decant reaction tubes containing larvae into a 12-well plate.
Incubate larvae in the dark.
Monitor staining reaction every 15–30 min using a stereo microscope.
Stop the staining reaction by washing larvae 2× in PBST for 1 min each.
Store larvae in PBST at 4°C.
Wash larvae in 50% EtOH-PBST for 5 min.
Incubate larvae twice in 100% EtOH for 5–15 min each.
Wash larvae in 50% EtOH-PBST for 5 min.
Wash larvae four times in PBST for 5 min each.
Decapitate larvae and mount trunks in 75% glycerol on a microscope slide.
Cover samples with a coverslip and seal with transparent nail polish.
Fix zebrafish larvae with PFA after spinal cord lesion (0–2 dpl).
Permeabilize fixed larvae.
Probe permeabilized larvae with antibodies of interest.
Detect specific proteins in whole-mount zebrafish larvae using immunohistochemistry.
Transfer larvae to a 2 mL reaction tube using a transfer pipette.
Fix larvae in 4% PFA for exactly 1 hour.
Wash larvae twice in PBST for 1 minute each.
Incubate larvae in 25% MeOH-PBST for 5 minutes.
Incubate larvae in 50% MeOH-PBST for 5 minutes.
Incubate larvae in 75% MeOH-PBST for 5 minutes.
Incubate larvae in 100% MeOH for 5 minutes.
Store samples in 100% MeOH at -20°C if needed.
Transfer larvae to a plastic petri dish filled with 100% MeOH.
Remove heads and tails using micro scissors under visual control.
Transfer trunk tissue containing the lesion site to a new 1.5 mL reaction tube.
Incubate samples in 100% MeOH at -20°C for 14-18 hours.
Rehydrate samples by incubating in 75% MeOH-PBST for 5 minutes.
Rehydrate samples by incubating in 50% MeOH-PBST for 5 minutes.
Rehydrate samples by incubating in 25% MeOH-PBST for 5 minutes.
Wash samples twice in ddH2O for 5 minutes each.
Incubate samples in 100% acetone (pre-chilled to -20°C) at -20°C for exactly 10 minutes.
Aspirate acetone and wash samples in ddH2O for 5 minutes.
Remove as much acetone as possible from samples to reduce sticking to the tube wall.
Wash samples twice in PBST for 5 minutes each.
Aspirate supernatant using a transfer pipette pre-coated with PBST to avoid sample loss.
Discard supernatant into 50 mL conical centrifuge tubes filled with PBST.
Return accidentally withdrawn samples to the reaction tube.
Incubate samples in PBST containing 5–7.5 μg/mL Proteinase K for 15 minutes.
Wash samples twice in PBST for no more than one minute each.
Re-fix samples by incubating in 4% PFA for exactly 15 minutes.
Wash samples three times in PBTx for 10 minutes each on a see-saw rocking shaker with low agitation at approximately 10 rpm.
Incubate samples in IHC blocking solution for a minimum of one hour on a see-saw rocking shaker with low agitation at approximately 10 rpm.
Incubate samples in IHC blocking solution containing primary antibody at 4°C for a minimum of three nights on a see-saw rocking shaker with low agitation at approximately 10 rpm.
Wash samples 8× in PBTx for 15 min each on a see-saw rocking shaker with low agitation at ∼10 rpm.
Incubate in IHC blocking solution containing appropriate fluorescent secondary antibody at 4°C for 2 nights on a see-saw rocking shaker with low agitation at ∼10 rpm.
Protect the samples from light in subsequent steps.
Wash samples 6× in PBTx for 10 min each on a see-saw rocking shaker with low agitation at ∼10 rpm.
Wash samples 2× in PBS for 1 min each to dilute PBTx.
Mount larvae in 75% glycerol or commercially available antifade mounts on a microscope slide, cover with a cover slip, and seal with transparent nail polish.
Image samples with a laser scanning confocal microscope for high resolution.
